claim: U.S. Sen. Mitt Romney participated in a June 7, 2020 civil rights protest.
label: true
explain:
On June 7, 2020, U.S. Sen. Mitt Romney, R-Utah, marched with civil rights demonstrators in Washington, D.C., likely making him the first Senate Republican to participate in a mid-2020 wave of protests against police brutality.
Black Lives Matter. pic.twitter.com/JpXUFlxH2J
— Mitt Romney (@MittRomney) June 7, 2020

Romney joined thousands of demonstrators who flooded the streets of cities across the U.S., protesting racism and police brutality in a movement sparked by the killing of George Floyd, an unarmed Black man who died in custody on May 25, after former Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck for nearly 9 minutes. Chauvin, who is white, and three other officers were jailed and face charges stemming from the incident.
Viral video of Floyd pinned to the ground and exclaiming that he was unable to breathe until he lost consciousness sparked international protests centered around the Black Lives Matter movement.
Because Romney did participate in a protest and tweeted the words “Black Lives Matter” from his account on June 7, 2020, we rate this claim “True.”

Mitt Romney join anti–police brutality protester in Washington Sunday , a symbolic rebuke of not only the current state of police in the U.S. , but of President Donald Trump ’ s handling of the civil unrest in the wake of the killing of George Floyd in Minneapolis . On the 10th day of protest outside the White House , the Utah senator , wear a mask , spend an hour and a half at the demonstration near the Capitol , an aide say . Romney have step up and speak out against Trump in the past , most recently vote for his impeachment for abuse of power , but it fail to galvanize any meaningful principled opposition to the president . One need not look far than the NFL ’ s rapidly evolve stance on police violence and systemic racism , the same league that three year ago freeze out Colin Kaepernick for kneel in protest during the anthem and then condemn those who follow in his footstep . “ We , the National Football League , admit we be wrong for not listen to NFL player earlier and encourage all to speak out and peacefully protest , ” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell say on Friday . During an interview , Romney say he show up because “ we need to end violence and brutality , and to make sure that people understand that black life matter . ”
Romney ’ s affirmation that “ black life matter ” be further evidence of what have be a sweeping change in how much—though not all—of America view the Black Lives Matter movement and the issue that underpin it . ”
Whether Romney ’ s presence be significant or just symbolic likely depend on if it prompt others in his party to speak up .
